hook: Language was the doorway — not the house. **Vision, speech, and images make GenAI a full-sense system**, and every pipeline you built gains a pair of eyes and a voice.

scenes.title: Vision & OCR: the model that can look at your screenshots
scenes.sub: Multimodal input — one API call reads charts, scans, and whiteboards
scenes.narration: Multimodal models accept IMAGES alongside text in the same chat call — the API shape you know from GA-03 gains an image_url content block, nothing more. The architecture-relevant capabilities: DOCUMENT UNDERSTANDING — pass a PDF page or scan; the model reads tables, forms, handwriting — for messy real-world documents pair it with a layout-aware extractor (GA-29's Document Intelligence) — the service gives clean structure, the model gives judgment; CHARTS & DIAGRAMS — screenshots of dashboards, ER diagrams, error dialogs — 'why is this chart spiking' becomes a question you can ASK; and OCR-adjacent tasks — transcription of signs, labels, receipts — a vision call beats a classic OCR pipeline whenever context matters, because the model reads MEANING ('total including tax') not just characters. Architecturally: images consume tokens — a page photo is worth hundreds to thousands of tokens (AG-13's context budget), so downscale, crop to the region of interest, and batch pages deliberately. Cost and latency both scale with resolution — treat pixels like the scarce resource they are.

scenes.title: Vision call: read a chart, ask a question
scenes.body:
import base64
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()

img = base64.b64encode(open("dashboard.png", "rb").read()).decode()

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "text",
             "text": "This is a Grafana dashboard. (1) Which panel "
                     "spiked at 14:20? (2) What changed 5 minutes "
                     "before? Answer from the image only."},
            {"type": "image_url",
             "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{img}",
                           "detail": "high"}},   # low|high → token cost
        ],
    }],
)
# Same shape as every chat call in this course — the
# content array just grew a second block type.
# detail:'low' → ~85 tokens per tile; 'high' → ~30x more.
annot: The call shape is GA-03's — multimodal is an input-format change, not a new paradigm
detail:'low' vs 'high' is a cost dial — charts need high; signature detection needs low
'from the image only' is groundedness discipline — the same anti-hallucination instinct as GA-10's citations

scenes.title: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech: the telephony stack, rebuilt
scenes.sub: Whisper-class STT and neural TTS — transcription is a solved commodity
scenes.narration: Speech is two APIs wearing one UX. SPEECH-TO-TEXT — Whisper-class models transcribe audio with punctuation, speaker awareness, and code-switching between languages — operationally it's a solved commodity: send audio, get text, handle it with the WHOLE pipeline you've built — transcribe then retrieve (GA-10), then answer with guardrails (AG-09). Engineering notes: chunk long audio with overlap, timestamp output when you need alignment with video or recordings, and post-process with an LLM pass for domain terms — 'Kubernetes' never survives raw transcription. TEXT-TO-SPEECH — neural voices are now indistinguishable from studio recordings, with per-sentence style control — the pipeline: agent's text answer → TTS → audio to user. TTS latency is real-time-bound — you can't precompute a conversation, so per-sentence streaming (sentence → synthesize → play while next sentence generates) is the standard mitigation, the same perceived-latency trick as LLM token streaming (GA-07). And VOICE SELECTION is a product decision — the earlier user feedback about voice preference applies to every shipped product: give users a choice, default to unobtrusive.

scenes.title: STT in, TTS out — a voice sandwich around your agent
scenes.body:
import asyncio

async def voice_session(audio_stream):
    # 1 · STT: stream audio chunks, stream text back
    text_stream = stt.transcribe_stream(audio_stream)

    # 2 · your ENTIRE existing pipeline, unchanged:
    async for user_text in text_stream:
        reply = await agent.answer(      # RAG + guardrails + tools
            user_text, session_id=...)

        # 3 · TTS: sentence-by-sentence streaming
        async for sentence in split_sentences(reply):
            audio = await tts.synthesize(sentence, voice="nova")
            yield audio          # play now; next sentence synthesizes
                                 # while this one plays

# Latency budget (target ≤ 1.2s from end-of-speech):
#   STT finalization   ~250ms
#   agent first token  ~400ms  (GA-07 streaming)
#   TTS first sentence ~300ms
#   — each stage streams into the next; totals overlap.
annot: The agent in the middle is unchanged — voice is an adapter layer, not a rewrite
Sentence-level TTS streaming hides synthesis behind playback — GA-07's perceived-latency principle, audio edition
The latency budget table is what you put in the NFR section GA-30 taught you to write

scenes.title: Realtime voice agents: the conversation becomes the interface
scenes.sub: Speech-to-speech models erase the text layer — and change the architecture
scenes.narration: The newest capability tier is SPEECH-TO-SPEECH: models that listen to audio and respond in audio directly, keeping tone, pace, and emotion in the loop — sub-second response, natural interruption handling — the phone call with a machine finally stops feeling like a phone call with a machine. Architecturally it's a different topology from the STT→LLM→TTS sandwich: a PERSISTENT BIDIRECTIONAL STREAM replaces request/response — the client streams audio up, audio flows down — WebSocket infrastructure (PY-14's territory) carries it, with the realtime API handling the session: turn detection, interruption, voice selection. What changes in your system design: STATEFUL SESSIONS — a call is a long-lived connection with mid-call context — memory scoping from AG-17 applies per-call; INTERRUPTION SEMANTICS — barge-in means the model must handle half-finished thoughts — treat it as a cancellation event (AG-19's abort discipline); and LATENCY BUDGETS collapse — the whole loop — hear, think, speak — now targets ~1 second, which rules out naive chains. Design pattern: keep the realtime model as the conversational FRONT DOOR, and hand structured work — lookups, transactions — to the text pipeline as TOOL CALLS — best of both topologies.

scenes.title: Realtime session: one stream, both directions
scenes.body:
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
client = AsyncOpenAI()

async with client.beta.realtime.connect(
        model="gpt-4o-realtime") as conn:
    await conn.session.update(
        voice="alloy",
        instructions="You are LKG's study concierge. Keep answers "
                     "under 30 seconds of speech. If a learner asks "
                     "about progress, call get_progress.",
        tools=[get_progress_schema],        # tools: SAME AG-16 contracts
    )

    async for event in conn:               # one loop, both directions
        if event.type == "response.audio.delta":
            speaker.play(event.delta)      # stream audio out
        elif event.type == "response.function_call":
            # structured work still goes through the text pipeline
            result = await handle_tool(event)   # RAG, guardrails, all
            await conn.conversation.item.create(result)
        elif event.type == "input_audio_buffer.speech_started":
            speaker.flush()                # barge-in → cancel playback
            # AG-19's abort discipline, conversational edition
annot: Tools ride along inside the realtime session — AG-16's registry pattern doesn't change
speech_started → flush playback: interruption is a first-class event, not an error
Instructions are a system prompt (GA-03) — plus a new constraint: answers sized in SECONDS of speech

scenes.title: Image generation: from prompt to pixels, and the architect's cautions
scenes.sub: Diffusion models draw; engineers decide where drawing belongs
scenes.narration: Image GENERATION — diffusion models turning prompts into pictures — is the most visually dramatic capability and the one needing the most architectural restraint. USE IT WHERE THE IMAGE IS THE PRODUCT: marketing variants, design drafts, synthetic data for training, illustrations from your own content pipeline. BE CAREFUL WHERE THE IMAGE CARRIES TRUTH: anything presented as evidence — the model invents plausible detail confidently, and a generated chart looks like DATA while being fiction — treat generated media like unvetted user input, watermark and label it (EU AI Act transparency duties), and never let it flow into your retrieval corpus unmarked (AG-22's injection lesson applies: an image full of text is an injection surface too). OPERATIONALLY: generation is slow and expensive relative to text — seconds per image, so ASYNC job patterns (AG-19) fit best; aspect/size parameters matter to downstream layouts; and editing modes — inpainting, variation — often serve products better than raw generation: the user's uploaded photo plus a small edit beats a full hallucinated scene. The architect's summary: text models REASON, image models RENDER — pipeline them in that order.

scenes.title: Generation as an async job — with labeling discipline
scenes.body:
async def generate_illustration(prompt: str, job_id: str):
    job = jobs.create(job_id)                # AG-19 async pattern
    img = await images.generate(
        model="dall-e-3",                    # or SDXL/Flux, self-hosted
        prompt=f"Flat vector style, brand palette: {prompt}",
        size="1792x1024",                    # downstream layout decides
        quality="hd",
    )
    stored = await storage.put(img, {
        "provenance": "ai-generated",        # label it — EU AI Act
        "watermark": "c2pa",                 # content credentials
        "prompt_hash": hash(prompt),
    })
    job.complete(stored.url)                 # webhook/PY-14 notifies UI

# Governance rules baked in:
#  • provenance metadata at birth — retro-labeling never happens
#  • generated media marked unsearchable until human review
#    (AG-22: an image of text is an injection vector)
annot: Async job pattern — seconds-long generation doesn't belong on a request thread (AG-19)
Provenance metadata at creation — the label is part of the artifact, not an afterthought
Mark generated media out of the RAG corpus until reviewed — injection defense from AG-22, media edition

recap: Vision is an input-format change: image_url content blocks in the same chat API — manage token cost with detail levels and cropping
Speech is a solved commodity — STT/TTS wrap your existing text pipeline; sentence-level TTS streaming hides latency behind playback
Realtime speech-to-speech replaces request/response with a persistent bidirectional stream — keep it as the conversational front door, route structured work through tool calls
Image generation renders but doesn't reason — pipeline text-first, run generation async, and label provenance at birth

quiz.q: Why does the STT → LLM → TTS sandwich architecture hide latency better than waiting for the full reply before synthesizing?
opts: TTS is faster on short sentences than long paragraphs
Sentence-by-sentence synthesis pipelines playback with generation — the user hears speech while later sentences are still being synthesized, so perceived latency is only first-sentence time
The network transfers audio faster than text
It doesn't — full-reply synthesis is always lower latency
quiz.why: Same principle as LLM token streaming (GA-07): time-to-first-signal dominates perceived latency. Playback of sentence N overlaps synthesis of sentence N+1 — total latency drops from 'synthesize everything' to 'synthesize first sentence'.

quiz.q: In a realtime speech-to-speech agent, what should happen when the user interrupts (barge-in)?
opts: Ignore it — the model should finish its current response
Treat it as a cancellation event: stop playback, flush the buffer, and let the new input start a fresh turn — interruption is a first-class event, not an error
quiz.why: AG-19's abort discipline, conversational edition: speech_started means cancel in-flight playback and generation, then process the new input. Latency budget ~1s total makes 'wait for politeness' impossible.

quiz.q: Why must AI-generated images be labeled with provenance metadata at creation time?
opts: An image can look like evidence while being fiction — labeling at birth satisfies transparency duties, prevents generated media from polluting retrieval corpora, and retro-labeling never actually happens
Labels make images smaller to store
It's only required for commercial use
quiz.why: Generated media presented as truth is a hallucination with pixels. Provenance (C2PA/watermark) at creation is the only reliable point to attach it — plus AG-22's angle: unlabeled generated images entering a RAG corpus are injection surfaces.

code.title: The multimodal pipeline, end to end
code.body:
# ONE pipeline, every sense:
async def handle(user_msg):
    # eyes: screenshots/charts/doc scans  (vision blocks)
    # ears:  audio → STT → text
    # brain: text + retrieved facts → answer   [UNCHANGED CORE]
    # voice: answer → sentence-TTS → stream
    # hands: tool calls for structured work
    # guardrails: screen every surface (AG-09)

    return pipeline.run(user_msg)

# The core you built in 76 reels didn't change.
# It just learned to see, hear, and speak.
annot: The brain is the text pipeline — multimodal layers are adapters around it
Every surface passes guardrails — image input, audio output, all of it (AG-09)
'Adapters around an unchanged core' — the sentence to remember in every architecture review

notes:
# Beyond Text — GA notes

## Vision & OCR
- image_url content blocks; detail low/high is the token-cost dial.
- Clean structure from Document Intelligence (GA-29) + judgment from the model.
- Ask 'from the image only' — groundedness discipline.

## Speech
- STT: commodity. Chunk long audio, timestamp, LLM post-pass for domain terms.
- TTS: per-sentence streaming hides latency behind playback.
- Voice is a product choice — offer options, default unobtrusive.

## Realtime voice agents
- Speech-to-speech, persistent bidirectional stream (WebSocket — PY-14).
- ~1s loop budget; interruption = cancellation event (AG-19).
- Pattern: realtime model as front door; structured work via tool calls (AG-16).

## Image generation
- Render, not reason — pipeline text-first.
- Async job pattern (AG-19); editing beats raw generation for products.
- Provenance at birth (C2PA, watermark); generated media out of RAG corpora until reviewed (AG-22); transparency duties under EU AI Act.
